You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Perhaps output: connect blocks? Hard to guess. Request a demo.

Analyze demo. Objects: regions of solid color (0-block, 1-blocks) separated by 3 background. In output, each block becomes solid: noise cells inside block region become the block color, and everything outside stays background 3. So rule: find rectangular solid blocks of one color; fill their bounding rectangle with that color; remove all other non-background noise.

Check demo: 0-block rows0-5, cols3-7 — output keeps as 0 in that rect (rows0-5 cols3-7 all 0). 1-block top-right: input rows1-5 cols12-17 color 1 with noise (5,6,4,8). Output rows1-5 cols12-17 all 1. Second 1-block rows14-17 cols3-9: input has 4s and 7 and 8 inside; output all 1. Noise like 8 at (4,1), 7 at (1,3)... wait 7 at (1,3) is inside 0-block rect? Row1 col3 is 7, inside 0-block; output row1 col3 = 0. Yes filled. Noise outside blocks → 3.

So rule: identify solid-color rectangular blocks; fill bounding rect with block color; all else → background 3.

Background determination: most frequent color = background (3 in demo, 6 in test). Blocks: connected regions of a single non-bg color forming near-rectangle? In test: 5-block rows5-10 cols6-11, with noise 4s inside (r5c9, r8c7, r9c11) → fill 5. 8-block rows3-4 cols15-21, noise 4 at r3c16 → fill 8. All scattered 4s elsewhere → 6.

But noise is same color as... noise in demo is various colors (5,7,8,4,6,1 inside blocks). Outside noise also. How to distinguish a noise cell of color 1 outside block? e.g. row14 "4 1 1 1 1 4 1 1" — the 4s at cols2 and 7 are inside block bounding box? Block is rows14-17 cols3-9. col2 row14 is 4 — outside block cols. In output row14 col2 = 3. And 8 at (16,8) inside → 1. 7 at (17,5) inside → 1.

But careful: noise 4s in test grid — could any be part of a block? Blocks are large connected solid regions. Noise 4s are isolated single cells. So: connected components of size >1 (or forming rect) with non-bg color = blocks; fill their bounding box. Isolated single cells = noise → bg.

Check demo: single cells like 8 at (4,1) isolated → 3. 5 at (0,11)? row0 col11 is 5, and row1 col13 is 5, col17 5... singles → bg. Component detection: 4-connected same color. The 0-block: all 0s connected. Good.

Edge: does filling use bounding box of the component? 0-block component: 0s at rows0-5 cols3-7 contiguous → bbox exactly. 1-block top-right: 1s rows1-5, cols12-17 → bbox. Works.

Test: implement.
